## US-0018 ? Smart Upgrade Mode
- user_visible: true
- Title: Safe, version-aware upgrade for repos already using its-magic
- Summary: When a user updates its-magic (e.g. `npm update -g its-magic`) and re-runs the installer on a repo that already has it, the current modes don't handle this well. `missing` skips changed files, `overwrite` destroys user data, `interactive` gives no context about what actually changed. A proper upgrade needs to distinguish between framework files (commands, rules, agents, hooks, skills, CI workflows, scripts) that should be updated and user data files (docs, sprints, handoffs, decisions, runbook, scratchpad) that should be preserved.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: Version tracking ? installer writes a `.its-magic-version` file (or similar) in the target repo recording the installed version.
  - [x] AC-2: File classification ? files are categorized as "framework" (safe to update) or "user-data" (preserve on upgrade).
  - [x] AC-3: New `--mode upgrade` (or equivalent) that updates framework files, preserves user data files, and warns about user-customized framework files that changed.
  - [x] AC-4: Upgrade summary ? after running, shows what was updated, what was preserved, and what needs manual attention.
  - [x] AC-5: New-file delivery ? new files added in a newer version are always copied (regardless of category).
  - [x] AC-6: Migration notes ? when file formats or required fields change between versions, guidance is provided (e.g. MIGRATION.md or inline notes).
  - [x] AC-7: Triple installer parity ? upgrade mode works identically across installer.ps1, installer.sh, and installer.py.
  - [x] AC-8: README documents the upgrade workflow.
- Notes: This addresses the gap where users who already use its-magic update the tool and need to propagate changes to their repos without losing sprint data, decisions, or runbook customizations.

## US-0021 ? Critical Evaluation in Intake and Architecture
- user_visible: true
- Title: AI challenges ideas, checks duplicates, and suggests alternatives before accepting
- Summary: Update the PO agent behavior and the `/intake` command so the AI does not blindly accept every idea. Before creating a backlog item, the AI should: (1) check if the idea is already covered by an existing story or decision, (2) evaluate whether the approach is sound or if a simpler/better alternative exists, (3) challenge assumptions and ask "is this the right solution or just the first one?", (4) only create a story after this evaluation passes. The same critical thinking applies to `/architecture` (challenge design decisions) and `/sprint-plan` (challenge task breakdown). `/intake` remains the single entry point for bugs, features, and improvements -- no need for separate `/bug` or `/feature-request` commands.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: PO agent checks backlog for duplicates/overlaps before creating new stories
  - [x] AC-2: PO agent evaluates feasibility and suggests alternatives when appropriate
  - [x] AC-3: PO agent challenges assumptions ("is this the best approach?") before accepting
  - [x] AC-4: `/intake` command steps updated to include evaluation phase
  - [x] AC-5: `/architecture` command steps updated to include design challenge phase
  - [x] AC-6: PO and Tech Lead agent definitions updated with critical evaluation behavior
  - [x] AC-7: Evaluation is constructive, not blocking -- good ideas proceed faster, weak ideas get improved

## US-0049 ? Legacy DONE-Story Acceptance/Traceability Backfill Guard
- user_visible: true
- Title: Guard and one-time backfill for backlog DONE vs acceptance/traceability drift
- Summary: Add deterministic detection and bounded repair for legacy stories where canonical backlog shows DONE but acceptance checkmarks or traceability/release artifacts disagree. Include optional one-time backfill mode, ongoing guard at reconciliation/release boundaries, explicit audit report entries and reason codes, and template parity plus regression coverage expectations.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Notes: Context: US-0017 and US-0030 were DONE in backlog but unchecked in acceptance and not clearly represented in traceability/release artifacts. Per R-0023. Released S0028 2026-03-02.
- Discovery notes:
  - Detection rule: legacy drift = backlog status DONE and (acceptance item unchecked OR traceability index/state lacks entry OR release artifacts lack clear representation for that story).
  - One-time backfill: explicit trigger runs detection and repair once; emits audit report; idempotent when no drift. Ongoing guard: at release/reconciliation (or dedicated check) detects drift and either blocks with reason code or performs target-scoped repair with audit append.
  - Audit report: canonical artifact (e.g. docs/engineering/legacy-drift-audit.md) with story ID, prior acceptance/traceability state, resolved state(s), reason code, evidence ref.
  - Reason codes: BACKLOG_DONE_ACCEPTANCE_UNCHECKED, BACKLOG_DONE_TRACEABILITY_MISSING, BACKLOG_DONE_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_MISSING (or equivalent) with remediation per code.
  - Boundaries: target-scoped repair only; no change to canonical status ownership (US-0045) or broad reconciliation semantics (US-0043). Template parity and regression coverage required.
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: Define and document detection rule: story is "legacy drift" when backlog status is DONE and (acceptance checklist item for that story is unchecked OR traceability index/state lacks entry OR release artifacts lack clear representation for that story).
  - [x] AC-2: Bounded target-scoped repair: normalization mutates only stories that match the legacy-drift rule; no broad destructive rewrite of unrelated backlog/acceptance/state/release artifacts.
  - [x] AC-3: Audit report format is defined with required fields: story ID, prior acceptance state, prior traceability state, resolved state(s), reason code, evidence reference; report written to a canonical artifact (e.g. `docs/engineering/legacy-drift-audit.md` or equivalent).
  - [x] AC-4: Reason-code vocabulary includes at least: `BACKLOG_DONE_ACCEPTANCE_UNCHECKED`, `BACKLOG_DONE_TRACEABILITY_MISSING`, `BACKLOG_DONE_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_MISSING` (or equivalent), with remediation guidance per code.
  - [x] AC-5: Optional one-time backfill mode: explicit trigger (e.g. command or flag) runs detection and repair once for all current legacy-drift stories and emits the audit report; idempotent and safe when no drift exists.
  - [x] AC-6: Ongoing guard: at release or reconciliation boundaries (or dedicated check), workflow detects legacy drift and either blocks with reason code and remediation or performs target-scoped repair with audit append; behavior is documented and deterministic.
  - [x] AC-7: Template parity: active and `template/` command/rule/docs guidance for backfill guard, audit report location, and reason codes remain behaviorally aligned.
  - [x] AC-8: Regression coverage includes at least: (a) one-time backfill run with no drift (no changes, report empty or "no drift"), (b) one-time backfill run with one legacy-drift story (repair applied, audit entry created), (c) ongoing guard blocks or repairs when drift is present and reports reason code.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: detection rule, target-scoped repair, audit report schema, reason codes, one-time backfill and ongoing guard behavior, template parity, regression tests.
  - Out of scope: changing canonical status ownership (US-0045), broad reconciliation semantics (US-0043), or runtime product feature behavior.

## US-0069 ? Strict Phase Role Enforcement in /auto Orchestration
- user_visible: true
- Title: Fail closed when /auto cannot run a phase with its required role capability
- Summary: Prevent role collapse (for example execute running as tech-lead) by enforcing deterministic phase-to-role mapping in `/auto`, with hard fail-fast behavior when the required role capability is unavailable.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Discovery notes:
  - User reported a generated repository run where `/auto` performed intake and then coding under tech-lead context instead of routing through intended phase roles.
  - Existing contracts define per-phase role intent, but capability enforcement is inconsistent across phases and can permit unintended fallback behavior in some repos.
  - User authority evidence: user explicitly requested intake to close this orchestration gap.
  - Discovery refinement (US-0069-only): enforce **preflight** role-capability resolution before each phase spawn; post-hoc evidence alone is insufficient.
  - Discovery refinement (US-0069-only): for phases with allowed role alternates, require **deterministic policy + precedence** so expected role is single-valued at each boundary.
  - Discovery refinement (US-0069-only): reject checkpoint completion when `role` in isolation evidence conflicts with the phase contract (fail-closed mismatch).
  - Discovery refinement (US-0069-only): align `proof_hash`/strict-proof `role` with the same resolved canonical role as isolation evidence for auditable linkage.
  - Discovery refinement (US-0069-only): default-deny non-`dev` execute contexts unless a documented override contract exists.
  - Research refinement reference (US-0069-only): `R-0048`.
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: Define canonical deterministic phase->role mapping contract for `/auto` (`intake=po`, `discovery=po`, `research=po|tech-lead` per policy, `architecture=tech-lead`, `sprint-plan=tech-lead`, `plan-verify=qa|tech-lead` per policy, `execute=dev`, `qa=qa`, `verify-work=qa`, `release=release`, `refresh-context=curator|po` per policy).
  - [x] AC-2: `/auto` must fail closed with deterministic reason code when required phase role capability is unavailable (no implicit fallback to unrelated role).
  - [x] AC-3: Boundary validation must reject phase completion evidence when `role` does not match expected role contract for that phase run.
  - [x] AC-4: Deterministic diagnostics must include phase id, expected role, actual role/capability result, and remediation guidance.
  - [x] AC-5: `/execute` specifically must never run under tech-lead context unless explicitly allowed by a documented override contract (default deny).
  - [x] AC-6: Resume/continuation logic preserves role enforcement; stale resume sources cannot bypass role checks.
  - [x] AC-7: Active/template parity is maintained for `/auto`, phase command docs, and related runbook/readme guidance.
  - [x] AC-8: Regression coverage includes capability-available pass path, missing-capability fail-fast path, role-mismatch checkpoint rejection, and no-silent-fallback assertions.
  - [x] AC-9: Reason-code vocabulary for role enforcement is deterministic and documented (for example `PHASE_ROLE_CAPABILITY_MISSING`, `PHASE_ROLE_MISMATCH`).
  - [x] AC-10: Release/readiness artifacts include auditable references proving required phase roles were used for completed lifecycle boundaries.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: orchestration role mapping, capability enforcement, and evidence validation contracts.
  - Out of scope: changing product/business implementation semantics of generated repositories.

## US-0070 ? Configurable Auto Phase Selection Policy

  - Discovery refinement (US-0070-only): resume and backlog-drain/bulk/team modes must persist and re-validate the same phase-policy inputs so skipped phases do not ?reappear? silently on continuation.
  - Discovery refinement (US-0070-only): operator-visible breadcrumbs should list **selected phases**, **skipped phases + reason** (`default_full_plan`, `policy_exclude`, `non_skippable_gate`, etc.), and invalid-token **fail-fast codes** (unknown phase id, empty plan, policy conflict).
  - Research follow-up (US-0070-only): `/research` should produce a precedence matrix, default non-skippable phase set, named profile sketch, and explicit compatibility notes with the `US-0069` phase?role contract (skipping a phase must not substitute roles or bypass capability gates).

  - Architecture refinement reference (US-0070-only): `DEC-0052`.

  - [x] AC-3: Unknown or invalid phase identifiers in policy fail closed with deterministic diagnostics (no silent ignore).
  - [x] AC-4: Safety-critical gates cannot be bypassed silently; policy defines which phases are non-skippable by default and why.

## US-0081 ? First-Intake Full-Plan Coverage and Story-Map Gate
- user_visible: true
- Title: Enforce complete plan coverage during first broad intake
- Summary: When intake scope is first/new/broad, PO must capture coverage for the complete user-provided plan as an explicit story map before persistence. Intake may still sequence delivery in steps, but every major plan area must be represented by a bounded story set (or explicitly deferred with rationale) so no broad-plan area is silently dropped.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** - policy gate, intake evidence contract, and regression checks should land together to avoid partial enforcement.
  - **Rationale**: splitting policy from validator/tests risks accepting broad intakes without enforceable coverage mapping.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0051** (DONE): broad-intake decomposition exists, but does not require explicit complete-plan coverage accounting.
  - **US-0068** (DONE): mandatory question packs enforce topic coverage, but not full-plan story-map coverage.
  - **US-0078** (DONE): interaction evidence gate validates questionnaire evidence, not plan-area completeness.
  - **Decision**: create a focused extension story to close the broad first-intake coverage gap.
- Discovery notes:
  - Intake closure (2026-03-31, PO, manual run): user reports first broad intake produced only one small story despite a complete software plan.
  - User authority evidence: user explicitly requires first intake to cover all plan areas, even when implementation is phased.
  - Policy intent: decomposition remains bounded (2-5 typical), but completeness accounting is mandatory.

## US-0083 ? Delegable Intake Clarification Without Hard Blocks
- user_visible: true
- Title: Make intake questions adaptive and explicitly delegable
- Summary: Improve intake so questions stay context-aware instead of feeling rigid/repetitive, and let users explicitly delegate unresolved decisions to the agent when they choose to skip details. The intake gate should remain safe/auditable, but explicit delegation must provide a non-blocking path instead of repeatedly halting progress.

## US-0084 ? POSIX npm installer + Linux remote test targets (WSL / SSH / Docker)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Reliable global `its-magic` install on Debian `/bin/sh` and automatable Linux/Docker test connectivity for dev/QA
- Summary: Close the gap where globally npm-installed `installer.sh` still fails under dash (`set: Illegal option -`) on SSH/Docker hosts, and give dev/QA a canonical, automatable way to aim tests and workflow phases at WSL, SSH Linux hosts, or container contexts?without inventing a parallel remote contract that conflicts with **`US-0064`** / **`release-targets.json`**.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? npm publish surface, installer POSIX guarantees, remote ergonomics, and regression tests are one delivery slice; splitting would leave broken global installs or undocumented remote paths.
  - **Rationale**: operators hit install failure before any remote feature matters; remote docs must reference the same config families already in the kit.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0008** (DONE): CLI installer exists; this story **repairs/extends** npm-published payload and CI guardrails, not a second installer.
  - **BUG-0004** (DONE): tracked `installer.sh` POSIX startup; **regression** may still occur in **published** tarballs?this story **locks publish-time parity** and diagnostics.
  - **US-0064** (DONE): remote connectivity schema exists; this story **adds dev/QA-oriented bootstrap** (WSL/SSH/Docker operator flows, optional probe script, scratchpad/remote.json hints) **aligned** to that contract?not a competing schema.
  - **US-0036** / **REMOTE_EXECUTION**: extend only as needed; preserve fail-fast validation and zero overhead when remote is off.
- Discovery notes:

Framed on top of the **US-0089** **shipped surface** (`.cursor/rules/caveman.mdc`, scratchpad keys `CAVEMAN_MODE` / `CAVEMAN_LEVEL`, and reserved no-op keys `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_INPUT` / `CAVEMAN_FILE_SCOPE` per **`DEC-0072`** 3; 9-zone literal-region invariant per **`DEC-0072`** 4; `TOKEN_PROFILE` x `CAVEMAN_MODE` non-substitution per **`DEC-0072`** 1). **Problem framing**: operators want bounded, reversible **input-side** token reduction for **agent-readable prose files** (docs, long-form handoffs) without ever silently mutating canonical workflow artifacts or secrets. **UX / operator flow**: operator flips **`CAVEMAN_MODE=1`** + sets **`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_INPUT=1`** + fills **`CAVEMAN_FILE_SCOPE`** with an explicit allow-list (globs or doc-root anchor ? exact grammar **architecture-locked**); runs a deterministic **`scripts/`** entrypoint (name **architecture-locked**; candidate prefix `caveman_compress_*`) in **`dry-run`** first; reviews a diff/inventory; optionally runs in **`write`** mode which **creates or updates a sidecar original** (path pattern **architecture-locked**; candidate `.<name>.caveman-original.<ext>` or sibling `caveman-originals/` folder ? research to evaluate); **never** touches files outside the allow-list or inside the hard deny-list. **Assumptions**: (1) Compression is **prose-only** (per upstream **JuliusBrussee/caveman** README discipline and **`R-0073`** finding: "compress touches prose, not code blocks") ? fenced code blocks, AC checklists, reason codes, IDs, contract markers, strict-proof tuple fields, isolation evidence fields, and git refs are **byte-preserved** (same 9-zone invariant as **`DEC-0072`** 4 ? reused verbatim so operators see one invariant, not two). (2) **Originals are preserved** for every write; `dry-run` never writes. (3) Compression is **idempotent** (re-running on an already-compressed file is a no-op; architecture/tests confirm). (4) No **`package.json`** / **`npm`** dep; pure Python under **`scripts/`**. (5) Exit-code + **reason-code** contract for every violation (e.g. `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_SCOPE_VIOLATION`, `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_DENY_HIT`, `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_NOT_IDEMPOTENT`, `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_LITERAL_REGION_DAMAGED`, `CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_ORIGINAL_MISSING` ? final names **architecture-locked**). **Hard deny-list (PO expectation baseline ? architecture can only broaden with explicit decision gate)**: (a) **`.env`** / `.env.*` / any path listed in **`.cursorignore`** / **`.gitignore`** secret patterns (**US-0085**); (b) **`handoffs/intake_evidence/*.json`** and sibling evidence bundles (**US-0078** / **DEC-0060** integrity ? **`BUG-0007`** class risk); (c) **`docs/product/backlog.md`**, **`docs/product/acceptance.md`**, **`docs/engineering/state.md`**, **`docs/engineering/decisions.md`**, **`decisions/DEC-*.md`** (canonical workflow authority ? **US-0045** status authority + **DEC-0040** artifact ordering); (d) **`sprints/*/plan-verify.json`**, **`sprints/*/uat.json`**, **`sprints/*/summary.md`**, **`sprints/*/release-findings.md`** (sprint-lifecycle evidence); (e) any **binary** (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.pdf`, `.zip`, ?); (f) **`package.json`**, **`package-lock.json`**, **`installer.*`**, **`.github/workflows/*.yml`**, **`.cursor/hooks/*.py`**, **`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`**, **`.cursor/commands/*.md`**, **`.cursor/skills/**/SKILL.md`** (contract surfaces ? Caveman voice composes with them; compression must not rewrite them). **Allow-list candidates (explicit opt-in via `CAVEMAN_FILE_SCOPE` only)**: long-form prose under **`docs/user-guides/`**, **`docs/engineering/runbook.md`** (prose paragraphs only; tables + code blocks untouched), archive packs under **`docs/engineering/state-archive/`** (cold artifacts; still sidecar-preserved), long-form PO?TL archive packs under **`handoffs/archive/*.md`**. Architecture decides whether the allow-list is **pure opt-in** (default empty; operator must supply scope explicitly) or ships a **named profile** (candidate `docs-prose-only`) ? **PO recommendation: pure opt-in default** for safety. **Risks**: (R1) Accidental rewrite of a canonical artifact if a glob is too broad ? **mitigation**: hard deny-list is **script-enforced** before any scope glob is evaluated; deny always wins over allow. (R2) Sidecar drift / orphaned originals if file is later moved ? **mitigation**: sidecar pattern architecture-locked; optional `--verify-originals` subcommand listed as research ask. (R3) Non-idempotent compression corrupting on second run ? **mitigation**: dedicated idempotency unit test per **AC-6**; architecture decides algorithm (whitespace-collapse, filler-word strip, header-preservation only). (R4) Violating the 9-zone literal-region invariant from **`DEC-0072`** 4 ? **mitigation**: reuse the same invariant (single source of truth); architecture may extend but MUST NOT narrow; test parity in `tests/` asserts identical zone list. (R5) Operators conflating **`TOKEN_PROFILE=lean`** with **`CAVEMAN_COMPRESS_INPUT=1`** ? **mitigation**: docs restate **`DEC-0072`** 1 non-substitution verbatim for the input-side axis too (voice vs context-breadth vs file-compression are **three independent axes**; architecture may publish as a compact 2x2x2 matrix or three parallel paragraphs). ## US-0091 ? README ? backlog/acceptance feature coverage backfill + blocking drift gate
- user_visible: true
- Title: One-time backfill of missing user-visible feature descriptions in the README family, plus blocking release-gate extension to prevent future drift
- Summary: Audit `README.md` against the canonical user-visible feature inventory in `docs/product/backlog.md` and `docs/product/acceptance.md`, backfill missing descriptions across the full README family (root `README.md`, `template/README.md`, and `docs/developer/README.md` per `DEC-0059`), and ship a deterministic feature-coverage validator wired into `/release` so the README cannot fall behind shipped user-visible features again. Composes on `US-0030` (command/flag doc-delta gate) and `US-0077` (audience profile) without rewriting either.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? operator explicitly chose `story_split=single`. Audit, backfill, and blocking drift guard ship together so the validator is wired the same sprint the catalog is populated; splitting risks shipping a guard that immediately blocks all future releases against an empty backfill, or shipping a backfill that drifts again before the guard lands.
  - **Rationale**: validator + backfilled catalog form one atomic contract; single story keeps the gate deterministic on first activation.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0030 (DONE)**: release gate that blocks `/release` when commands/flags **changed** without README/runbook updates. **Distinct**: `US-0030` is delta-driven; `US-0091` is static-coverage-driven. `US-0091` composes as a **second check** inside the same `/release` doc-delta gate surface, sharing remediation guidance vocabulary.
  - **US-0077 (DONE) / DEC-0059**: dual-README audience strategy (`USER_*` H2s in root `README.md`, `DEV_*` H2s in `docs/developer/README.md`). **Distinct**: `US-0077` defines structure/audience; `US-0091` populates it for missing user-visible features. Backfilled blurbs MUST respect existing `USER_*` / `DEV_*` H2 vocabulary and section budgets ? no new audience surfaces invented.
  - **US-0017 (DONE)**: template-drift guard for active vs `template/`. **Compose**: feature-coverage validator reuses `US-0017` parity rather than duplicating it.
  - **US-0071 (DONE)**: user-visible metadata sanitization. **Compose**: backfilled wording remains subject to `US-0071` scanning surfaces; no internal planning tokens leak into operator-visible blurbs.
- Operator intake answers (per AskQuestion 2026-05-10):
  - `scope_files=both` ? root `README.md` AND `template/README.md` (parity preserved).
  - `audience_focus=both_profiles` ? `USER_*` blurbs in root + `DEV_*` rows in `docs/developer/README.md` (DEV shard) + `template/` mirrors.
  - `feature_set=user_visible` ? only user-visible features / commands / flags / DONE bug fixes that affected operator behavior; pure-internal guards / refactors are out of scope.
  - `drift_guard=blocking` ? extend `/release` doc-delta gate as a blocking check.
  - `story_split=single` ? single story.
  - `priority=P1`.
- Intake-time research (DEC-0011): **`R-0074`** ? README ? backlog/acceptance coverage gap surface, validator placement options, release-gate composition with `US-0030`, parity composition with `US-0017`, audience boundaries with `US-0077`/`DEC-0059`.

  - [x] AC-3: **Backfill** lands in the three target files: root `README.md`, `template/README.md` (byte parity per `US-0017`), and `docs/developer/README.md` for developer-profile rows.   - [x] AC-4: Audience boundaries are preserved ? `USER_*` H2 vocabulary (root) and `DEV_*` H2 vocabulary (DEV shard) per `DEC-0059` are not invented or renamed; section budgets per `validate_doc_profile.py` cells are respected.

- Boundaries:

## US-0092 ? Full-autonomy `/auto` mode + outer driver + self-verification
- user_visible: true
- Title: Opt-in full-autonomy orchestration ? shipped outer driver, self-build/self-test UAT, block auto-resolve, drain-without-pause, and TOKEN_PROFILE token-cost-only orthogonality
- Summary: Close the gap left by **US-0088** where continuous `/auto` and backlog drain are **documented** but Cursor often stops after one phase or one US/bug segment unless the operator manually re-invokes `/auto`. Ship an **opt-in** **`AUTO_FLOW_MODE=full_autonomy`** (exact literal **architecture-locked**) that: (1) runs a **stdlib outer-driver script** (not operator-only manual re-invocation) until a deterministic stop; (2) expands **verify-work** / **QA** to **self-execute** UAT and operator-manual steps via build, test, API, browser, or stack-appropriate probes (**US-0065** / **US-0066** composition); (3) **auto-remediates** transient blocks within bounded caps instead of stopping for operator tick; (4) **advances** to the next OPEN story or bug without waiting when segment completes and drain policy allows; (5) **audits and fixes** any docs/scratchpad text implying **`TOKEN_PROFILE`** changes automation level ? **`TOKEN_PROFILE` controls context breadth / token cost only** (operator requirement). Default-off; **`auto_until_decision`** and **`manual`** remain unchanged.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story (PO default)** ? outer driver, flow mode, UAT self-verify, block retry, drain-without-pause, and TOKEN_PROFILE orthogonality audit ship as one vertical contract so downstream repos get one upgrade path. TL may split at **`/architecture`** only with explicit user authority if sprint sizing forces it.
  - **Rationale**: Shared stop matrix, scratchpad keys, and contract tests must stay coherent; partial delivery risks repos enabling flags without the outer driver or self-verify path.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0088 (DONE)**: continuous multi-phase + quiet drain ? **US-0092** **extends** with shipped outer driver and full_autonomy semantics; does not weaken spawn-only (**BUG-0006**).
  - **US-0044 (DONE)**: backlog drain switches ? **US-0092** makes drain **operator-less** when full_autonomy enabled.
  - **US-0065 / US-0066 (DONE)**: runtime QA autopilot + generated tests ? **US-0092** generalizes self-verify for UAT/manual steps beyond generated-project scope where stack profile resolves.
  - **US-0080 (DONE) / DEC-0062**: token-cost profiles ? **US-0092** **clarifies** TOKEN_PROFILE must not gate automation; audit removes conflicting prose.
  - **US-0087 (DONE)**: bug-queue mode ? full_autonomy composes; scheduler mutex unchanged.
- Intake-time research (DEC-0011): **`R-0078`** (stub at intake ? extend in **`/discovery`** / **`/research`**) ? outer-driver design, full_autonomy stop matrix vs US-0088, UAT self-verify probe catalog, block-retry ledger, TOKEN_PROFILE orthogonality audit scope.
- Acceptance:

## US-0093 ? Cursor browser-integrated UAT self-test (browser_smoke + automatable manual UI)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Self-test web apps via Cursor built-in browser ? execute browser_smoke/manual UI probes, complete probe stubs, evidence in uat.json
- Summary: Close the gap left by **US-0092** / **DEC-0078** where **`browser_smoke`**, **`process_health`**, and **`cli_smoke`** probes classify acceptance steps but **`scripts/uat_probe_lib.py`** returns **`UAT_PROBE_UNRESOLVED`** without execution, and **`manual_operator`** UI/workflow steps are never auto-run. Ship a vertical contract so **`/verify-work`**, **`/qa`**, and **`/execute`** (webapp contexts) drive **Cursor built-in browser** tools (navigate, click, type, scroll, screenshot, console/network evidence) as the **primary** web self-test path, with deterministic **HTTP / Playwright subprocess fallback** when browser MCP is unavailable. Automate **manual_operator** steps that describe UI workflows (not human-judgment-only). Record path-ref evidence in **`uat.json`** `probe_results[]` and **`qa-findings.md`**; fail closed with explicit reason codes ? **no silent PASS**.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story (PO default)** ? browser execution, manual UI routing, stub completion, agent-command contract, evidence schema, and docs/tests parity ship as one upgrade path composing on **US-0092**.
  - **Rationale**: Probe catalog, reason codes, and command contracts must stay coherent; partial delivery risks repos marking browser UAT PASS while probes remain stubs.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0092 (DONE) / DEC-0078**: probe catalog + fail-closed vocabulary ? **US-0093** **implements** execution for **`browser_smoke`** and completes **`process_health`** / **`cli_smoke`** stubs; does not weaken security deny-list or spawn-only (**BUG-0006**).
  - **US-0065 (DONE)**: webapp runtime QA browser guidance ? **US-0093** wires Cursor browser as the concrete automation path.
  - **US-0088 / US-0092 full_autonomy**: self-verify during `/qa` and `/verify-work` ? browser probes must compose without false PASS.
  - **R-0041**: Cursor Browser tools cited ? **US-0093** delivers integration contract.
- Intake-time research (DEC-0011): **`R-0079`** (stub at intake ? extend in **`/discovery`** / **`/research`**) ? Cursor browser MCP agent contract vs stdlib fallback, manual_operator UI routing rules, evidence schema, security/approval posture.

## US-0094 ? README visionary intro + tiered feature hierarchy (root/template parity)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Rewrite README opening for autonomous AI dev team positioning ? framework purpose first, main features, sub-features, then preserved detail
- Summary: The root `README.md` opening still reads like a generic template blurb and buries the product story: **you are the customer/dreamer**; an **AI dev team** (PO, Tech Lead, Dev, QA, Release, Curator) runs intake ? discovery ? architecture ? sprint ? execute ? QA ? release with **artifact-first memory** and optional **full autonomy** (`AUTO_FLOW_MODE=full_autonomy`, **US-0092**). Re-audit against all user-visible **US-xxxx** / **BUG-xxxx** items (**US-0091** / **DEC-0074**), then restructure the top of the README family: **(1)** framework purpose and operator role, **(2)** main capability pillars, **(3)** sub-capability groupings, **(4)** existing detailed sections (`Setup`, `How-to`, `Commands and workflow`, walkthroughs, etc.) unchanged in substance below. **`README.md`** and **`template/README.md`** must remain **byte-identical** (**US-0017**). Composes on **US-0091** (coverage catalog must survive), **US-0077** / **DEC-0059** (USER_* H2 vocabulary), **US-0092** (full-autonomy messaging).
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? intro rewrite, tiered hierarchy, coverage re-audit, and root/template parity ship as one atomic README contract; splitting risks a visionary intro that immediately fails **US-0091** coverage or diverges active/template copies.
  - **Rationale**: operator asked for one coherent README narrative plus identical files; hierarchy without parity or coverage is incomplete delivery.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0091 (DONE) / DEC-0074**: static feature-coverage backfill + blocking gate ? **distinct**: **US-0091** ensured every shipped item has an anchor; **US-0094** improves **information architecture** and **product positioning** at the top without removing anchors. Re-run **`validate_readme_feature_coverage.py`** after edit.
  - **US-0077 (DONE) / DEC-0059**: dual README strategy ? **compose**: keep USER_* H2 literals; tiered intro may add **subsections** (`###`) under existing H2s but must not invent new top-level audience H2s or exceed section budgets.
  - **US-0017 (DONE)**: template drift ? **compose**: byte parity between root and `template/README.md` is an explicit acceptance criterion.
  - **US-0092 (DONE)**: full autonomy ? **compose**: intro must foreground opt-in autonomous team operation (`/auto`, backlog drain, outer driver) as a primary value prop, not a footnote.
- Intake-time research (DEC-0011): **`R-0080`** ? README narrative hierarchy patterns for autonomous dev frameworks; pillar grouping for 90+ feature anchors; Diataxis-style lead vs reference body separation (**R-0054** precedent).
- Baseline audit (intake, 2026-06-07): `python scripts/validate_readme_feature_coverage.py --report` ? **`coverage_missing=[]`**, **`coverage_total=104`**; root and `template/README.md` already byte-identical ? work is restructure + copy, not net-new coverage items.

  - [x] AC-1: **Framework purpose lead** ? new opening (before or within first `## Features`) states: operator as customer/dreamer; AI role-based team; artifact-first repo memory; phased workflow from `/intake` through `/release`; optional full autonomy (`AUTO_FLOW_MODE=full_autonomy`) as opt-in headline capability (**US-0092**).

## US-0095 ? Native in-Cursor `/auto` auto-chaining (no outer driver required)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Cursor-native continuous `/auto` ? in-chat phase and backlog-drain chaining without `auto_outer_driver.py`
- Summary: Close the operator-experience gap left by **US-0092** / **DEC-0078** where **`AUTO_FLOW_MODE=full_autonomy`** + **`AUTO_BACKLOG_DRAIN=1`** still stops at **`stop_reason=completed (segment exhausted)`** after a single Cursor `/auto` turn and tells the operator to re-run `/auto` or **`python scripts/auto_outer_driver.py`**. Ship a **Cursor-native auto-chain** contract so one `/auto` orchestrator invocation **continues in-chat** across (1) **all intersected lifecycle phases** per **US-0088** reference Step 5, and (2) **backlog-drain segment boundaries** (next OPEN story/bug) **without** requiring the stdlib outer driver or manual re-invocation between segments ? while preserving **spawn-only** orchestration (**BUG-0006** / **US-0069**), isolation (**US-0048**), strict proof (**US-0056**), and the **US-0088** / **US-0092** hard stop matrix. **`scripts/auto_outer_driver.py`** remains as an **optional** headless/CI fallback, not the primary IDE path when **`full_autonomy`** is enabled.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story (PO default)** ? native in-chat chaining, drain-advance-without-pause in IDE, docs/runbook/contract-test updates, and outer-driver demotion to fallback ship as one vertical contract; partial delivery risks operators enabling **`full_autonomy`** without actual in-chat continuation.
  - **Rationale**: Shared stop matrix, spawn boundary, and operator messaging must stay coherent; splitting risks docs claiming native chaining while behavior still requires the outer driver.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0092 (DONE) / DEC-0078**: shipped outer driver + **`full_autonomy`** ? **US-0095 extends** with **primary IDE path** = in-chat auto-chain; does **not** remove outer driver or weaken spawn-only.
  - **US-0088 (DONE)**: continuous multi-phase + drain ? **US-0095** closes the **Cursor single-turn** gap that **US-0088** documented as outer-driver equivalence (Option B).
  - **US-0044 (DONE)**: backlog drain ? **US-0095** makes drain **in-chat** when **`full_autonomy`** enabled.
  - **US-0087 (DONE)**: bug-queue ? composes; scheduler mutex unchanged.
  - **US-0023 (DONE)**: fresh subagent per phase ? **compose**: auto-chain must **spawn** phase roles, not execute phases in orchestrator turn.
- Intake-time research (DEC-0011): **`R-0081`** (stub at intake ? extend in **`/discovery`** / **`/research`**) ? Cursor-native continuation model (orchestrator self-chain vs Task/subagent scheduling), segment drain advance in IDE, interaction with caps, outer-driver fallback boundary.
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: **`/auto`** command + **`auto-orchestration-reference.md`** define **native in-chat auto-chain** when **`AUTO_FLOW_MODE=full_autonomy`**: orchestrator **must not** stop after one phase or one story segment solely due to Cursor turn boundaries; continuation uses documented Cursor-native mechanism (e.g. orchestrator schedules next phase spawn or next drain segment **within the same `/auto` run**).
  - [x] AC-2: **Drain-without-pause (IDE)**: with **`full_autonomy`** + **`AUTO_BACKLOG_DRAIN=1`** (or bug-queue per **US-0087**), segment completion (**`refresh-context`** boundary) **immediately** schedules the next OPEN item **in-chat** ? no operator message requiring **`auto_outer_driver.py`** or manual re-`/auto` for the default IDE recipe.
  - [x] AC-3: **Spawn-only preserved**: orchestrator turn still **must not** execute phase-role work (**BUG-0006**); each phase completes only via fresh subagent spawn + artifacts; contract tests regress **US-0069** preflight/post checks.
  - [x] AC-4: **Stop matrix unchanged for hard gates**: **`decision_gate`**, isolation/strict-proof violations, security deny, **`BACKLOG_MAX_STORIES_REACHED`**, **`AUTO_LOOP_MAX_CYCLES`**, unrecoverable **`error`**, **`pause_request`** ? still hard stop in IDE path; relaxable transient stops per **US-0092** matrix when configured.
  - [x] AC-5: **Outer driver demoted to fallback**: runbook + README family state **`scripts/auto_outer_driver.py`** is **optional** for headless/CI/`--invoke-cmd` automation ? **not** required for IDE **`full_autonomy`**; remove or rewrite prose that implies outer driver is mandatory for drain.
  - [x] AC-6: **Operator surface**: segment handoff may still notify when **`AUTO_QUIET=0`**; when **`AUTO_QUIET=1`**, suppress routine per-phase chatter but **do not** emit stop-and-wait instructions to run outer driver between segments under **`full_autonomy`**.

- Summary: Close the token-cost gap left by **US-0080** / **DEC-0062** (context breadth via **`TOKEN_PROFILE`**) and **DEC-0052** (phase exclusion reinstatement blocks naive skips): ship a new **`DELIVERY_MODE`** scratchpad axis (**`standard`** \| **`ultra_lean`** \| **`mega_quick`**, default **`standard`**) that controls **lifecycle shape and artifact surface** while preserving near-same code quality. **`ultra_lean`** collapses eleven canonical phases into **four macro-phases** (`spec` ? `plan` ? `build+verify` loop ? `ship`) with **`work/US-xxxx/pack.json`**, **`handoffs/active-context.md`**, and **section-scoped narrow-read** of vision/architecture/decisions ? **not** amnesia. **`mega_quick`** routes **`/auto`** to enhanced **`/quick`** semantics for small work. **Tranche A** universal wins (narrow-read in all commands, tighter default hot surfaces, delta handoffs, touch-graph reads) ship **without** mode opt-in. **`DELIVERY_MODE=standard`** remains **byte-compatible** with today's full lifecycle, gates, and **DEC-0052** reinstatement.

## US-0097 ? Project-owned root README bootstrap + per-story/sprint growth (framework README in `its_magic/` only)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Separate framework README from project README ? bootstrap repo overview at project start and extend it on every shipped story/sprint
- Summary: Complete the **US-0062** / **DEC-0045** ownership split: **`its_magic/README.md`** is the only installer-delivered **framework** catalog; **root `README.md`** is **project-owned** and must be bootstrapped on first project story and extended on each shipped user story or sprint with a user-facing repo overview plus developer orientation. Refactor doc gates so **US-0091** static coverage applies to the **framework** README family (not the project root), and add a **project README** validator + **`/execute`** / **`/release`** mandatory steps (default-on) so operators no longer inherit a 1600-line its-magic README in new repos and never manually chase README drift.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? installer boundary, migration, bootstrap scaffold, phase wiring, gate separation, and validators ship as one vertical slice; partial delivery risks repos that stop shipping framework README to root but still lack project README automation.
  - **Rationale**: Operator pain spans install payload, lifecycle phases, and validation; splitting installer from execute gates would leave the observed gap (framework README at root, no growing project README) partially unresolved.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0062 (DONE) / DEC-0045**: declared **`its_magic/README.md`** as framework surface ? **US-0097 completes delivery** (root still receives framework README via manifest today).
  - **US-0091 (DONE) / DEC-0074**: framework feature coverage in README family ? **distinct**: **US-0097** scopes **US-0091** to framework paths and adds **project** backlog ? root README coverage.
  - **US-0077 (DONE) / DEC-0059**: dual-audience **framework** docs ? **compose**: project README uses a **simpler** user + developer section model for **product** content, not framework `USER_*`/`DEV_*` catalogs.
  - **US-0032 (DONE)**: optional per-feature guides at **`docs/user-guides/US-xxxx.md`** ? **distinct** (optional, not root README); **US-0097** is default-on project overview at root.
  - **US-0030 (DONE)**: command/flag delta gate ? **compose** unchanged for framework surfaces; project README gate is additive.
- Intake pack evidence (**first-intake-pack**, **US-0081** / **DEC-0064** plan map):
  - `selected_pack=first-intake-pack`
  - `asked_topics=` all eight first-intake keys covered
  - `missing_topics=(none)`
  - `assumptions_confirmed=(none)`
  - `plan_area_inventory` / `plan_area_coverage` / `coverage_complete=true` ? all seven areas map to **`US-0097`**
  - `intake_evidence_ref=handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0097-intake-20260613.json`
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: **Installer ownership** ? **`docs/engineering/context/installer-owned-paths.manifest`** no longer treats root **`README.md`** as framework install payload (framework catalog ships only under **`its_magic/README.md`** + **`template/its_magic/README.md`** parity); fresh **`missing`** install on an empty target does **not** lay down the its-magic framework README at repo root.
  - [x] AC-2: **Non-destructive migration** ? **`upgrade`** / documented migration lifts legacy framework root **`README.md`** into **`its_magic/`** (or replaces root with a minimal project pointer) **without** deleting operator-authored project prose when detectable; deterministic reason codes + runbook remediation for ambiguous merges.
  - [x] AC-3: **Project README bootstrap** ? on first **`/execute`** completion for a **project** story when root **`README.md`** is missing or matches a framework-placeholder sentinel, materialize a **project scaffold** (title from **`docs/product/vision.md`**, purpose blurb, empty feature catalog marker, user + developer sections).
  - [x] AC-4: **Per-story/sprint delta** ? **`/execute`** (and **`/release`** when story ships) **requires** updating root **`README.md`** with at least one user-facing blurb for the target **`US-xxxx`** (and sprint summary cross-link when applicable); fail-closed reason family when delta skipped.
  - [x] AC-5: **Audience structure** ? project README documents **(a)** end-user repo overview (what the product does, how to run/use) and **(b)** developer orientation (setup, layout, where code/tests live); framework commands catalog remains only in **`its_magic/README.md`** (optional one-line pointer from project README allowed).
  - [x] AC-6: **Gate separation** ? **`validate_readme_feature_coverage.py`** ( **US-0091** ) validates **framework** README paths only; new **`validate_project_readme_coverage.py`** (name locked in architecture) validates **project** DONE **`user_visible`** backlog rows against root **`README.md`**; umbrella + sub-codes documented.
  - [x] AC-7: **Release composition** ? **`/release`** runs project README gate (scratchpad **`PROJECT_README_ENFORCE=1`** default after bootstrap) alongside existing framework gates; **`PROJECT_README_ENFORCE=0`** records skipped evidence during migration only.
  - [x] AC-8: **Metadata hygiene** ? project README edits pass **`check-user-visible-metadata.py`** (**US-0071**); no internal planning tokens in operator-facing project blurbs.
  - [x] AC-9: **Contract tests + template parity** ? harness markers for installer manifest, migration sentinel, execute/release mandatory steps, and project validator; **`check_intake_template_parity.py --scope=project-readme`** (or equivalent manifest) **PASS**.
  - [x] AC-10: **Architecture + runbook** ? **`decisions/DEC-xxxx.md`** + **`docs/engineering/architecture.md`** **`# US-0097`** document ownership matrix, placeholder detection, tranche order (A installer ? B bootstrap ? C phase wiring ? D validators), and operator troubleshooting; active + **`template/`** command/runbook parity.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: installer/manifest, migration, project README bootstrap + deltas, phase command wiring, project validator + release gate, framework/project gate separation, tests/parity/runbook.

## US-0098 ? Dev environment auto-launch profile (detect, persist, relaunch, connect)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Auto-detect developer runtime, persist profile, rebuild/relaunch after execute changes, and surface connection parameters
- Summary: Close the gap where **US-0065** / **US-0086** / **US-0067** validate or route at **workflow phase boundaries** but do **not** continuously **rebuild, restart, and reconnect** the app in the **detected dev environment** after implementation changes. Ship a **scratchpad-gated dev auto-launch profile** (default-off) so **`/execute`** (and optional explicit operator refresh) can: **(1)** detect **local**, **docker-host-local** (shell/`docker` on the same machine), or **automation remote** targets; **(2)** **persist** an operator-seeded **dev-environment profile** the agent reuses; **(3)** run **bounded** container rebuild / process restart recipes; **(4)** present **operator-ready connection info** (URL/host:port, health path, service/container id) with **names-only** secret refs ? composing with **US-0064**, **US-0085**, **US-0086**, and existing **`DEV_SERVER_*`** scratchpad keys without reading **`.env`**.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? profile schema, detection heuristics, execute relaunch contract, container orchestration, operator connection surface, and docs/tests ship as one vertical slice; partial delivery risks persisted profiles without safe relaunch or relaunch without connection reporting.
  - **Rationale**: Operator pain spans detection, persistence, rebuild, and UX; splitting profile from relaunch would leave ?AI remembers env but never restarts? partially unresolved.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0065 (DONE) / DEC-0047**: phase-gated runtime QA startup ? **distinct**: **US-0098** targets **dev-loop relaunch during execute**, not only QA/verify verdict evidence.
  - **US-0086 (DONE)**: automation remote **test routing** ? **compose**: shared heuristics; **US-0098** adds **dev profile persistence + relaunch + connection surfacing**, not **`TEST_COMMAND`** reroute alone.
  - **US-0067 (DONE) / DEC-0049**: release **Run/Connect/Verify** hints ? **distinct**: **US-0098** surfaces connection info **during development**, not at release finalization.
  - **US-0085 (DONE) / DEC-0071**: **`.env`** exclusion ? **US-0098** must inherit (no AI read; env-ref names only in persisted profile).
  - **US-0064 (DONE)**: connectivity schema unchanged ? **US-0098** maps to existing target ids / **`*Env`** indirection.
  - **US-0093 (DONE)**: **`process_health`** / **`DEV_SERVER_COMMAND`** ? **compose**: relaunch may feed probes; **US-0098** owns profile + rebuild orchestration.
- Intake pack evidence (**first-intake-pack**, **US-0081** / **DEC-0064** plan map):
  - `selected_pack=first-intake-pack`
  - `asked_topics=` all eight first-intake keys covered
  - `missing_topics=(none)`
  - `assumptions_confirmed=(none)`
  - `plan_area_inventory` / `plan_area_coverage` / `coverage_complete=true` ? all eight areas map to **`US-0098`**
  - `intake_evidence_ref=handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0098-intake-20260613.json`
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: **Scratchpad + `template/`** define an explicit **dev auto-launch profile** (architecture-locked flag names, default **off**); when **off**, manual daily dev workflows remain **unchanged** (no mandatory relaunch overhead).
  - [x] AC-2: **Dev-environment profile schema** ? committed template + operator-writable persisted profile (path **architecture-locked**, e.g. **`.cursor/dev-environment.json`**) with **names-only** secret refs; operator may seed once; agent updates idempotently with evidence; **no** inline secrets in git-tracked JSON.
  - [x] AC-3: **Environment detection** ? deterministic labels at minimum **`local`**, **`docker-host-local`**, **`docker`**, **`ssh`** (or architecture-locked synonym table); **docker-host-local** = direct shell/`docker`/`docker compose` on the dev machine (not remote SSH); fail-closed reason codes when profile/stack unresolved.
  - [x] AC-4: **`/execute` relaunch contract** ? when dev auto-launch profile is **on** and implementation touches documented runtime/container surfaces, run **bounded** rebuild/restart (e.g. **`docker compose build`** + **`up`**, or stack-aware dev server restart); record relaunch evidence in **`handoffs/dev_to_qa.md`** (command, mode, outcome, retry count).
  - [x] AC-5: **Operator connection surface** ? after successful relaunch, emit deterministic **Connect** block for the operator (URL or **`host:port`**, health check path, service/container/target id, runtime mode); **no** secret values; align field shapes with **`runtime-connectivity.md`** where applicable.
  - [x] AC-6: **Composition** ? reuse **US-0086** routing precedence where automation remote is enabled; inherit **US-0085** **`.env`** exclusion; extend **`DEV_SERVER_COMMAND`** / **`DEV_SERVER_PORT`** semantics documented in scratchpad; do **not** replace **US-0064** JSON schema.
  - [x] AC-7: **Explicit refresh path** ? document operator phrase and/or command hook (architecture-locked) to **refresh dev environment** without waiting for execute task completion; fail-closed when profile disabled or target unroutable.
  - [x] AC-8: **Bounded safety** ? retry/relaunch caps, non-transient fail-fast (e.g. missing compose file, disabled target), deterministic reason-code family (e.g. **`DEV_ENV_PROFILE_*`**, **`DEV_ENV_RELAUNCH_*`**); no unbounded file-watch daemon in v1 unless architecture documents a safe bounded trigger.
  - [x] AC-9: **Contract tests + template parity** ? stdlib helper self-test (if shipped), command/runbook markers, **`check_intake_template_parity.py --scope=dev-environment`** (or equivalent manifest) **PASS**.
  - [x] AC-10: **Architecture + runbook** ? **`decisions/DEC-xxxx.md`** + **`docs/engineering/architecture.md`** **`# US-0098`** document profile schema, detection matrix, execute relaunch triggers, docker-host-local vs remote semantics, troubleshooting; active + **`template/`** parity.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: dev profile schema/persistence, detection heuristics, execute-phase relaunch, container rebuild recipes, operator connection surfacing, scratchpad gates, optional stdlib helper, docs/tests/parity.
  - Out of scope: replacing **US-0064** schema; production deploy/release orchestration; unsupervised infinite watch loops; reading **`.env`**; mandating remote setup for manual daily work.

- Title: Configure LLM model strength per its-magic phase/role via stable tiers and optional local slug catalog
- Summary: Close the operator gap where **all** subagent phases inherit one parent model or ad-hoc **`model:`** slugs in **`.cursor/agents/`** ? with no framework contract for **cheap vs strong** models per lifecycle phase, no protection against **volatile model IDs** in template files, and no documented **API-only / BYOK** caveats when Cursor subagents may not route through custom API keys. ## US-0102 ? Direct per-phase model slug override and role-based catalog presets (US-0101 extension)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Extend US-0101 tier-based model selection with direct per-phase slug override and role-based catalog presets, while retaining 3-tier baseline
- Summary: US-0101 delivered per-phase `MODEL_TIER_<PHASE>` (cheap/balanced/strong) ? Cursor alias mapping (fast/inherit) with optional local catalog for vendor slugs. Operators now request a second axis: **direct per-phase model slug assignment** (`MODEL_<PHASE>=<vendor-slug>`) that bypasses the tier indirection layer, plus **role-based catalog presets** (PO/SA/DEV/QA model profiles per `ai_modell_auslegung_cursor_highend.md`) for operators who want curated model sets without manual tier mapping. The 3-tier system remains as the default/fallback layer: **precedence** `MODEL_<PHASE>` > `MODEL_TIER_<PHASE>` > `MODEL_TIER_DEFAULT` > Cursor alias (local catalog or stable alias). The `/ask` phase (already in US-0101 default matrix as `cheap`) is reinforced with direct override support. **Compose with US-0101/DEC-0086** (do not amend ? US-0101 stays DONE). **Backward compatible**: tier-only configurations continue to work unchanged. **No volatile vendor IDs in template files** ? direct slug keys and role-based presets live in local catalog JSON (gitignored) only; templates keep Cursor-stable identifiers. New catalog schema v2 extends v1 with optional `roles` section. New contract tests `test_us0102_*` validate precedence, schema, backward compatibility.
- Priority: P2
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? direct override scratchpad keys, precedence logic, catalog schema v2, role-based presets, backward compatibility, validator updates, contract tests ship as one vertical slice; splitting would ship override logic without catalog integration or reverse.
  - **Rationale**: "tier system stays default; advanced operators can assign exact models per phase or pick a role-based preset" without breaking US-0101 DONE status or forcing tier users to migrate.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0101 / DEC-0086 (DONE)**: per-phase tier selection ? **compose, do not amend**: US-0101 stays DONE; US-0102 adds a second overlay axis (direct slug override + role-based catalog). Precedence documented: `MODEL_<PHASE>` > `MODEL_TIER_<PHASE>` > `MODEL_TIER_DEFAULT` > Cursor alias. No changes to US-0101 ACs or DEC-0086 locks.
  - **US-0080 / DEC-0062 (DONE)**: `TOKEN_PROFILE` ? **orthogonal**: direct slug override still selects LLM identity (not context breadth); non-substitution paragraph in runbook.
  - **US-0003 (DONE)**: subagent definitions ? **unchanged**: template agents keep Cursor-stable aliases; direct slugs and role presets live in local catalog only (no volatile vendor IDs in templates).
  - **US-0092 / DEC-0078 (DONE)**: outer driver / SDK agents ? **distinct**: document optional per-send `model` for programmatic paths; out of scope for mandatory IDE resolver v1.

## US-0103 ? AI Decision Ledger + Plan Fidelity policy
- user_visible: false
- Title: Append-only ledger of every AI deviation and plan-fidelity scratchpad tri-state
- Summary: Sovereign-loop foundation - every AI decision made while running autonomously must be auditable. New handoffs/sovereign_decisions/<orchestrator_run_id>.jsonl records each decision as {ts, role, decision_id, type, from_artifact, to_artifact, rationale, plan_fidelity, cross_model_reviewed, risk_tier}. Governed by AUTO_PLAN_FIDELITY=strict|relaxed|extended: strict = hard stop on deviation, relaxed = AI may drop/reorder ACs, extended = AI may add new stories/features. QA cross-checks the ledger at every /qa boundary. Default-off AI_DECISION_LEDGER=0|1. Compose with US-0070/US-0048/US-0069 (do not amend).
- Priority: P0
- Status: DONE (2026-06-28)
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** - audit ledger + plan-fidelity policy are one vertical capability; splitting would orphan the ledger or the governance.
  - **Rationale**: "Every autonomous AI decision must be recorded and auditable; plan-fidelity governs what deviations are allowed."
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0070 (DONE)** / **US-0048 (DONE)** / **US-0069 (DONE)** / **US-0092 (DONE)**: phase selection policy, isolation evidence, phase role enforcement, full-autonomy outer driver - **compose, do not amend**: sovereign loop adds ledger + plan-fidelity governance ON TOP of resolved_phase_plan.

## US-0104 ? Cross-Model Adversarial Critic
- user_visible: false
- Title: Per-phase cross-model critic subagent with Challenger/Architect/Subtractor lenses + anti-slop scoring
- Summary: After each phase-role subagent completes, sovereign loop optionally spawns a critic subagent using a different model from the producer. The critic evaluates through one of three lenses: Challenger (edge cases, race conditions), Architect (coupling, boundaries), Subtractor (over-engineering, premature abstraction). Findings reconcile via parallel jury: agreement = high-confidence; single-finder = flagged. New field model_id in isolation evidence. Anti-slop scoring (per-lens 0-N score; below threshold results in rework loop). Falls back to single-model-multi-lens when only one model CLI installed. Compose with US-0048/US-0069/US-0110.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE (2026-06-29)

  - [x] AC-2: `/sovereign-critic` command + template mirror; `/auto` orchestrator hook after producer phase when enabled.

## US-0105 ? Sovereign Memory
- user_visible: false
- Title: Project-level learnings substrate injected into phase spawns
- Summary: New `docs/engineering/sovereign-memory/` directory with `decisions-log.jsonl`, `mistakes.jsonl`, `patterns.jsonl`, `plan-drift-register.jsonl`, and `retrospectives/<sprint_id>.md`. Bounded injection at phase spawn: top-N recent + top-K high-impact entries via `scripts/sovereign_memory_lib.py`. Token/char budget enforced per **US-0080** / **DEC-0062**. Curator **`/refresh-context`** writes retrospective after each release and may promote ledger highlights. Dedup on `decisions-log.jsonl`. Mistake-tagging on failed fix/revert. Default-off **`SOVEREIGN_MEMORY=0|1`**. Compose with **US-0029** / **US-0080** / **US-0103** (do not amend).
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE (2026-06-29)
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? directory schema, JSONL write paths, bounded injection lib, curator retrospective hook, dedup/mistake-tagging, and contract tests ship as one vertical capability; partial delivery risks operators enabling injection without schema validation or char-cap enforcement.
  - **Rationale**: Institutional memory only helps when writes, reads, and injection limits are coherent; splitting schema from injection reintroduces token-cost and hallucination risk.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0029 (DONE)**: external web research in `docs/engineering/research.md` ? **compose, do not amend**; sovereign memory holds **internal project learnings**, not web citations (may reference `R-xxxx` IDs as provenance only).
  - **US-0080 (DONE) / DEC-0062**: token-cost hardening ? **compose** via **`SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS`** bounded digest injection; does not change **`TOKEN_PROFILE`** or slim-command contracts.
  - **US-0096 (DONE) / DEC-0082**: per-story lean memory (`work/US-xxxx/pack.json`, `handoffs/active-context.md`) ? **distinct layer**; sovereign memory is **cross-run project-level** substrate, not a fourth triad member.
  - **US-0103 (DONE) / DEC-0103**: per-run audit ledger (`handoffs/sovereign_decisions/<orchestrator_run_id>.jsonl`) ? **compose** via optional promotion hook at refresh-context; **does not amend** 12-field ledger schema.
  - **US-0024 (DONE)**: memory-drift audit ? **distinct**; drift audit compares artifacts vs codebase; sovereign memory records delivery learnings.
  - **US-0107 (DONE)**: drain-generate consumer ? reads sovereign memory via lib API; drain-generate orchestration delivered in S0107.
- Acceptance:
  - [x] AC-1: Scratchpad keys `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY=0|1` (default `0`), `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_TOP_N` (default `5`), `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_TOP_K` (default `3`), `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS` (default `2048`); when `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY=0`, zero overhead ? no JSONL writes, no injection reads, no spawn digest assembly.
  - [x] AC-2: Directory `docs/engineering/sovereign-memory/` (+ `template/` mirror) with four JSONL artifacts (`decisions-log.jsonl`, `mistakes.jsonl`, `patterns.jsonl`, `plan-drift-register.jsonl`), `retrospectives/` subdirectory, and `.gitkeep` parity; deterministic v1 field contracts per artifact family documented in architecture.
  - [x] AC-3: `scripts/sovereign_memory_lib.py` (+ template mirror) exposes bounded injection API: merge **top-N recent** (by `ts` desc) + **top-K high-impact** (by `impact_score` desc from `patterns` + `mistakes`); dedupe by `entry_id`; truncate to `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS`; return names-only digest (no secret-shaped literals).
  - [x] AC-4: Phase spawn integration ? when `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY=1`, subagent spawn context includes read-only **`sovereign_memory_digest`** block assembled by lib (compose **US-0023** fresh-context semantics ? digest is additive read-only input, not a phase-role change).
  - [x] AC-5: Curator **`/refresh-context`** after release writes `docs/engineering/sovereign-memory/retrospectives/<sprint_id>.md` with sprint summary, learnings pointers, and optional promotion of ledger highlights into `decisions-log.jsonl` when `AI_DECISION_LEDGER=1`.
  - [x] AC-6: Dedup on `decisions-log.jsonl` via normalized `decision_key` (SHA-256 prefix); append rejected with `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_DECISION_DUPLICATE`. Mistake-tagging hook writes `mistakes.jsonl` entries on failed fix/revert events (orchestrator-detectable reason codes: `FIX_FAILED`, `REVERT_APPLIED`, `PLAN_FIDELITY_VIOLATION` family).
  - [x] AC-7: Eight `test_us0105_*` contract markers covering scratchpad keys, JSONL schemas, injection char cap, dedup branch, mistake-tagging literals, zero-overhead default, compose guards; parity `check_intake_template_parity.py --scope=sovereign-memory` (`SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_PAIRS`).
  - [x] AC-8: Architecture `# US-0105`, runbook operator recipe, `SOVEREIGN_MEMORY_*` reason-code inventory, template byte-parity; compose regression guards **`test_us0105_us0029_compose_no_research_schema_change`**, **`test_us0105_us0080_injection_respects_char_cap`**.

- user_visible: false
- Title: Per-role objective + inter-role review obligations bootstrappable from single YAML

Validator **`scripts/sovereign_role_manifest_validate.py --self-test`**. Lib **`scripts/sovereign_role_manifest_lib.py`** for objective injection + obligation dispatch. Default-off **`SOVEREIGN_ROLE_MANIFEST=0|1`**. Compose with **US-0069** (phase?role matrix unchanged ? manifest layers objectives and cross-role reviews on top of preflight enforcement).
- Priority: P2

YAML schema, validator, objective injection, cross-role review dispatch, **`cross_model_policy`** compose with **US-0104**, and contract tests ship as one vertical capability; partial delivery risks operators enabling dispatch without schema validation or **`US-0069`** compose guards.

## US-0107 ? Sovereign Loop Mode (AUTO_SOVEREIGN)
- user_visible: false
- Title: Project-level autonomous delivery that owns backlog/deploy/convergence end-to-end
- Summary: New AUTO_SOVEREIGN=0|1 orthogonal to full_autonomy. Four capabilities: (a) deferral register (handoffs/sovereign_deferrals.jsonl bounded by AUTO_SOVEREIGN_DEFERRAL_MAX); (b) drain-generate (when portfolio empty + convergence not met, PO-loop spawn creates candidate stories from vision + sovereign-memory; operator decision gate per candidate); (c) notification (SOVEREIGN_NOTIFY_TARGET ntfy|email|hook on convergence or cap exhaustion); (d) self-healing deploy integration (defers to US-0109). Compose with US-0088/US-0092/US-0095/US-0103/US-0105/US-0110 ? **do NOT amend** US-0088/US-0092/US-0095.

- Status: DONE (2026-06-29)

- Title: Multiple dev subagents race on same task in isolated worktrees; QA critic picks winner
- Summary: Under SOVEREIGN_PARALLEL_DEV=1, execute spawns N (bounded, default 3) parallel dev subagents in isolated git worktrees with different models/lenses. QA cross-reviewer evaluates all N outputs; passing one selected (first PASS + highest anti-slop score; ties break by earliest proof_issued_at). Merge via AUTO_SOVEREIGN_MERGE_RESOLVE=first_pass_wins|last_pass_wins|manual. Resource guard AUTO_SOVEREIGN_PARALLEL_MAX_TOTAL=6. Compose with US-0047/US-0092.
- Priority: P2
- Status: DONE
- Acceptance (8 ACs): SOVEREIGN_PARALLEL_DEV scratchpad flag with N parameter, worktree isolation per subagent bounded by AUTO_SOVEREIGN_WORKTREE_MAX, selection predicate (first PASS + highest anti-slop), merge policy (first_pass_wins|last_pass_wins|manual), resource guard with cap, contract tests, backward compat (0 = single dev), documentation + template parity.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: parallel dev scratchpad flags, worktree isolation logic, selection predicate, merge policy, resource guard, contract tests, template parity.
  - Out of scope: changing US-0047/US-0092 semantics; mandatory QA/release gate weakening; bulk execute changes.
- related_us: US-0047, US-0092, US-0103, US-0104, US-0107

## US-0112 ? Ship model-catalog example presets on install/upgrade
- user_visible: true
- Title: Installer delivers all model-catalog.local.example*.json presets on install and upgrade
- Summary: Close the operator gap after **US-0101** / **US-0102** / **DEC-0086** / **DEC-0087** where eight committed **`template/.cursor/model-catalog.local.example*.json`** presets (base, cursor-only, level 1?4, role-based balanced/highend) exist and are documented in scratchpad comments but **`installer-owned-paths.manifest`** omits them ? so **`missing`** and **`upgrade`** installs do not copy examples into consumer **`.cursor/`** repos. Operators enabling **`MODEL_RESOLVE=local_catalog`** or **`role_catalog`** must manually copy presets from the its-magic repo. Ship **framework example delivery**: add all eight example paths to **`[install_include_paths]`**; treat **`model-catalog.local.example*.json`** as **framework** files (refresh on **`upgrade`** when template changed, add on **`missing`** when absent); **never** copy or overwrite gitignored **`.cursor/model-catalog.local.json`** (operator active catalog). Composes with **US-0018** smart upgrade, **US-0075** example-first refresh posture, and **US-0099** install-bootstrap pattern (examples are framework-owned, not copy-when-missing for local catalog).

## US-0118 ? Work-kind classification + tiered delivery routing per story

- user_visible: true
- Title: Per-story work-kind classifier (doc / mini / code) driving tiered phase routing so small items skip overhead
- Summary: Today every `US-xxxx` story runs the same canonical lifecycle (or one global `DELIVERY_MODE`) regardless of whether it is a README tweak, a mini code fix, or a full feature. `DELIVERY_MODE` (US-0096 / DEC-0082) is a **global** scratchpad flag, not derived from the story's actual shape, so operators pay architecture / qa / verify-work overhead just to update a README. This story adds a deterministic **work-kind classifier** `scripts/work_kind_classify_lib.py` that takes `(story prose, AC set, touched-file hints, component_scope)` and returns `work_kind ∈ {doc, mini, code}` plus a recommended `delivery_mode` and `resolved_phase_plan`. A new default-off scratchpad flag `WORK_KIND_ROUTING=0|1` gates the feature (zero overhead when off). Backlog rows gain optional `work_kind` and `recommended_delivery_mode` fields set at intake (operator accept/override) and consumed by `/auto` `resolve_delivery_mode` step 0. `doc` work-kind routes to `[intake, execute, release]` (skip discovery/research/architecture/sprint-plan/plan-verify/qa/verify-work); `mini` routes to `ultra_lean` or `mega_quick`-style; `code` keeps the full lifecycle. Reuses the existing `scripts/dev_environment_lib.py:classify_touched_files()` tier A/B/C + skip-prefix precedent. Composes (read-only) with US-0096 (delivery modes), US-0070 (phase selection), US-0078 (intake evidence), US-0051 (decomposition), US-0069 (phase->role matrix).
- Priority: P2
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? classifier lib + scratchpad flag + intake integration + `/auto` integration + reason codes + tests + parity ship as one vertical slice; splitting classifier from routing would leave `/auto` without a consumer and routing without a classifier.
  - **Rationale**: Operator pain is "I run the whole phase chain for a README update"; the fix is one coherent routing primitive end-to-end.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0096 / DEC-0082 (delivery modes)**: **compose not duplicate**. US-0096 provides global `DELIVERY_MODE` + `resolved_phase_plan` macro-phase collapse; US-0118 makes the routing **per-story** and **derived** from work-kind. US-0096 precedence wins when explicitly set; US-0118 only fills the unset case.
  - **US-0070 / DEC-0052 (phase selection policy)**: **compose**. `AUTO_PHASE_*` keys remain the explicit operator override; US-0118 derives a default `resolved_phase_plan` only when those keys are unset and `WORK_KIND_ROUTING=1`.
  - **US-0096 `mega_quick` routing**: **compose**. `mega_quick` eligibility checks (AC <= 3, no DEC, single component) overlap with `mini` work-kind signals; US-0118 classifier may recommend `mega_quick` for eligible `mini` items rather than inventing a fourth route.
  - **US-0051 / US-0078 (intake decomposition + evidence)**: **compose**. Classifier runs after ACs are drafted and after the decomposition evaluator, before persistence; evidence bundle records `work_kind` proposal + operator accept/override.
  - **`scripts/dev_environment_lib.py:classify_touched_files()`**: **reuse**. Existing tier A/B/C + `TIER_C_SKIP_PREFIXES` (`docs/`, `handoffs/`, `sprints/`, `decisions/`, `tests/`, `.cursor/commands/`, `template/docs/`) is the natural seed for `doc` work-kind detection.
- Intake pack evidence (first-intake-pack):
  - selected_pack: first-intake-pack
  - asked_topics: users_problem, runtime_target_environment, language_framework_runtime, architecture_preference, ui_design_expectations, security_compliance, non_functional_priorities, scope_timeline
  - missing_topics: (none)
  - assumptions_confirmed: (none)
  - intake_evidence_ref: handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0118-intake.json
  - plan_area_inventory: 1 row (`work-kind-classifier`)
  - plan_area_coverage: 1 row (`work-kind-classifier` -> story_ids=[US-0118])
  - coverage_complete: true
- Acceptance:
  - [ ] AC-1: **Classifier library** ? `scripts/work_kind_classify_lib.py` exposes `classify_work_kind(story_prose, acceptance_criteria, touched_file_hints, component_scope) -> WorkKindResult` returning `work_kind ∈ {"doc","mini","code"}`, `recommended_delivery_mode` (`standard`|`ultra_lean`|`mega_quick`), `recommended_phase_plan` (list of canonical phase ids), `rationale` (string), and `evidence_refs` (names-only). Pure stdlib, no network, no `.env` reads.
  - [ ] AC-2: **Classification rules** ? `doc` when all touched files match `dev_environment_lib.TIER_C_SKIP_PREFIXES` or are `*.md`/`README*` under skip prefixes -> phase plan `[intake, execute, release]` (skip discovery/research/architecture/sprint-plan/plan-verify/qa/verify-work). `mini` when single component, ACs <= 3, no companion DEC required -> `ultra_lean` or `mega_quick` (reuse US-0096 `mega_quick` eligibility). `code` otherwise -> `standard` (or current `DELIVERY_MODE`).

Active + `template/` parity.

## US-0119 ? Autonomous-autonomy presets and configurable hard-stop relaxation
- user_visible: true
- Title: AUTONOMY_PRESET scratchpad presets plus configurable relaxation of non-security hard stops for fully autonomous runs
- Summary: Today's `AUTO_FLOW_MODE=full_autonomy` / `SOVEREIGN_*` / `CROSS_MODEL_*` stack ships many hard-stop reason codes (`ARTIFACT_ORDERING_ANCHOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `STATE_TIMESTAMP_NON_MONOTONIC`, `ARTIFACT_HOT_SURFACE_OVERSIZE`, `RESUME_BRIEF_STALE`, `CROSS_MODEL_REWORK_CAP_EXHAUSTED`, `INTAKE_*_PACK_*`, `SOVEREIGN_DRAIN_*_BLOCKED`, `RELEASE_PUBLISH_*`, etc.) that are safe to auto-repair or soft-skip in a self-driving loop, but the governance layer refuses to do so. Operators also have to flip twelve individual autonomy flags (`INTAKE_AUTONOMY_MODE`, `WORK_KIND_AUTO_ACCEPT`, `RESUME_BRIEF_AUTO_REFRESH`, `CROSS_MODEL_SKIP_PHASES`, `SOVEREIGN_DRAIN_AUTO_ACCEPT`, `RELEASE_PUBLISH_AUTO_CONFIRM`, `RUNTIME_PROOF_KIND`, `GOAL_CONVERGENCE_INTERVAL`, `CROSS_MODEL_REWORK_EXHAUSTED_POLICY`, `AUTONOMY_STOP_POLICY`, `INTAKE_MINIMAL_PACK`, `INTAKE_ASSUME_STACK_CONTEXT`) to reach zero-touch flow. US-0119 adds a single `AUTONOMY_PRESET={none|balanced|full}` scratchpad flag whose value expands deterministically into a well-defined bundle of per-feature autonomy flags (all default-off individually so backward compatibility is preserved), plus an `AUTONOMY_STOP_POLICY={block|auto_repair_then_block|auto_repair_then_skip}` flag that classifies every fail-closed reason code as `security_hard` (never auto-resolved) or `autonomy_resolvable` (bounded auto-repair with a ledger before escalating). Compose (read-only) with US-0092/US-0095/US-0056/US-0068/US-0096/BUG-0007: the preset layer is additive only ? it expands into existing flags, it never rewrites their semantics.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** ? preset expansion + stop-class matrix + reason-code audit + per-feature flag wiring + backward-compat tests + scratchpad/template parity ship as one vertical slice.
  - **Rationale**: splitting stop-class matrix from preset expansion would leave presets without a policy engine; splitting individual feature flags from preset expansion would leave the single-flag operator value with no effectors.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0092 / US-0095 (full-autonomy + native chain)**: **compose not duplicate**. US-0092/US-0095 defined the orchestration layer; US-0119 adds a configurable relaxation layer on top.
  - **US-0096 (delivery modes)**: **compose**. Delivery-mode routing orthogonally decides *which* lifecycle runs; US-0119 only softens the governance gates around it.
  - **US-0056 (strict runtime proof)**: **compose**. Proof semantics unchanged; `RUNTIME_PROOF_KIND` only selects a lighter attestation inside autonomy mode.
  - **US-0068 (mandatory intake packs)**: **compose**. Pack schema unchanged; `INTAKE_AUTONOMY_MODE=1` and `INTAKE_MINIMAL_PACK` only relax the operator-question surface on known-stack repeat projects, never bypass the evidence gate.
  - **BUG-0007 (truthfulness)**: **compose**. Anti-echo rule unchanged; `INTAKE_ASSUME_STACK_CONTEXT=1` only auto-fills `language_framework_runtime`/`runtime_target_environment` rows from backlog history on established projects, with the `assumption_confirmation_ref` contract still enforced.
- Intake pack evidence (first-intake-pack):
  - selected_pack: first-intake-pack
  - asked_topics: users_problem, runtime_target_environment, language_framework_runtime, architecture_preference, ui_design_expectations, security_compliance, non_functional_priorities, scope_timeline
  - missing_topics: (none)
  - assumptions_confirmed: Stack is Python+Node.js; `AUTONOMY_PRESET=none` default is byte-identical pre-US-0119; security hard gates block under every preset; template parity preserved; sovereign-loop composes read-only; US-0092/US-0095/US-0056/US-0068/BUG-0007/US-0096 unchanged.
  - intake_evidence_ref: handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0119-intake-20260705.json
  - plan_area_inventory: 1 row (`autonomy-presets`)
  - plan_area_coverage: 1 row (`autonomy-presets` -> story_ids=[US-0119])
  - coverage_complete: true
- Acceptance:

When `none`, byte-identical pre-US-0119 behaviour. When `balanced` or `full`, deterministic expansion into per-feature autonomy flags documented in AC-2.
  - [ ] AC-2: **Deterministic preset expansion** ? `scripts/autonomy_preset_lib.py:expand_autonomy_preset(preset, overrides) -> dict` returns the flag bundle. Every preset line expands into already-existing scratchpad keys only; no new consumer semantics invented here. Explicit per-flag values in scratchpad (or scratchpad.local) always win over preset expansion.

Every fail-closed reason code classified in `docs/engineering/autonomy-stop-matrix.md` as `security_hard` (never auto-resolved) or `autonomy_resolvable` (bounded auto-repair with a ledger cap).

YAML companion `scripts/data/autonomy_stop_matrix.yaml` with `scripts/validate_autonomy_stop_matrix.py` enforcing (a) no orphan code in scripts, (b) `security_hard` rows carry `auto_repair_kind=n/a`, (c) `autonomy_resolvable` rows carry finite `cap`.

Contract test `test_us0119_security_hard_gates_never_auto_repaired` fails on divergence.
  - [ ] AC-8: **Bounded auto-repair ledger** ? new append-only file `handoffs/autonomy_repair_ledger/<orchestrator_run_id>.jsonl` recording one row per auto-repair attempt (`reason_code`, `auto_repair_kind`, `attempt`, `outcome`, `evidence_ref`). Cap per `(run, reason_code)` taken from matrix `cap` column (default 3). Cap exhaustion escalates with new terminal `AUTONOMY_REPAIR_CAP_EXHAUSTED` stop reason. File gitignored at the per-run path.
