## US-0120 — Separate `/closure` phase after `/release` with exclusive Story Closure responsibility
- user_visible: false
- Title: Separate `/closure` phase after `/release` with exclusive Story Closure responsibility
- Summary: Story Closure (Status DONE in `docs/product/backlog.md` + acceptance checkbox `[ ]`→`[x]` in `docs/product/acceptance.md` + state checkpoint traceability) is currently embedded in `/release` step 10–12. During the US-0119 lifecycle, the Release subagent claimed to have performed closure but the actual files were NOT modified (backlog.md remained OPEN, acceptance.md remained unchecked). This is the same "subagent execution fidelity" issue that blocked the Execute cycle. By extracting closure into a dedicated `/closure` phase with exclusive responsibility, we (1) reduce the scope of the release subagent so it focuses on release artifacts only, (2) give the orchestrator a verifiable closure checkpoint (similar to how we fixed execute-cycle fidelity), and (3) enforce "one phase, one responsibility" consistency across the lifecycle. New lifecycle structure (ultra_lean ship macro): `release → closure → refresh-context` (3 phases instead of 2). Compose (read-only) with US-0043/US-0045/US-0040/US-0048/US-0056/US-0096: `/closure` executes what US-0043 defines (reconciliation), follows US-0045 ownership rules (canonical status authority), operates after US-0040 release artifacts are written, produces its own US-0048 isolation evidence and US-0056 runtime proof, and applies to all delivery modes per US-0096.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- work_kind: doc
- recommended_delivery_mode: ultra_lean
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single story** — one focused lifecycle governance change with clear inputs (release evidence artifacts from prior `/release`) and outputs (status flip, acceptance check, state checkpoint, closure verification artifact).
  - **Rationale**: splitting closure command file from orchestrator wiring would leave closure unreachable from `/auto`; splitting release.md step 10–12 removal from new closure wiring would leave existing release subagents performing closure incorrectly.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0043 (backlog reconciliation contract)**: **compose not duplicate**. US-0043 defines WHAT reconciliation means; US-0120 creates a dedicated phase that EXECUTES reconciliation.
  - **US-0045 (canonical status source)**: **compose**. `/closure` follows US-0045 canonical status ownership rules (backlog is authority, acceptance + state are derived).
  - **US-0040 (release artifacts)**: **compose**. `/closure` operates AFTER release artifacts are written, not instead of them.
  - **US-0096 (delivery modes)**: **compose**. `/closure` applies to all delivery modes equally — every lifecycle has a closure step.
  - **US-0048 (isolation evidence)**: **compose**. `/closure` produces its own isolation evidence (fresh subagent per phase per BUG-0006).
  - **US-0056 (strict runtime proof)**: **compose**. `/closure` produces its own runtime proof.

## US-0121 — OpenCode template pack and installer host mode
- user_visible: true
- Title: Ship `template/.opencode/**` pack plus installer `--host cursor|opencode|both` without breaking Cursor
- Summary: Operators need its-magic on stock OpenCode without replacing the Cursor kit. This first vertical slice adds an empty-but-valid `template/.opencode/` tree (agents, commands, plugins, gitignore for local models/keys), copies it into consumer repos via the existing installer (`missing`/`upgrade`/`clean`), and adds `--host cursor|opencode|both`. Default remains **cursor-only until explicit opt-in**. Cursor coexistence is a hard gate: cursor-only install must not regress `.cursor/` delivery.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Epic**: six workflow-step slices **US-0121..US-0126** accepted via operator-submitted `docs/product/opencode-adapter-masterplan.md`.

  - **Split axis**: workflow steps (install → roles → models → spawn plugin → thin commands/validators → docs/tests), not technical layers.
  - **Rationale**: installer without a pack is empty; pack without installer never reaches consumer repos.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0008 (CLI installer)**: **compose, additive host mode only** — do not rewrite missing/overwrite/clean semantics.

## US-0122 — OpenCode role agents and Layer-1 permission table
- user_visible: true
- Title: Map seven its-magic roles plus orchestrator to OpenCode agents with host-enforced permissions
- Summary: Cursor rules are advisory. This slice maps **US-0003** roles (`po`, `tech-lead`, `dev`, `qa`, `release`, `curator`, `security`) plus an orchestrator (`auto`) onto OpenCode agents (markdown under `.opencode/agents/` and/or `opencode.json` `agent`). Layer 1 is the **permission table** (`allow`/`ask`/`deny` on `edit`, `bash`, `task`, …). Layer 2 prompts stay short (role + allowed artifacts only). Success test (c): a model that ignores its prompt still cannot let PO write production code if `edit` is `deny`.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - Independently valuable: operators can `@po` / Task-invoke roles with host permissions before the orchestrator plugin (US-0124) exists.
  - Does not clone `.cursor/agents/*.mdc` or dump command files into prompts.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0003**: **compose** — same role contract; new host files, not a 1:1 Cursor clone.
  - **US-0023 / BUG-0006**: isolation remains spawn-only; this story supplies per-agent permissions that the plugin (US-0124) will enforce for `/auto`.
  - **US-0002 / US-0004**: do **not** port Cursor rules/skills as the enforcement mechanism.

Orchestrator: `edit` deny (or equivalent no phase-artifact writes); `task` allow only for the seven role agents (glob / allow-list). `po`: `edit` allow only under `docs/product/**` and `handoffs/po_to_tl.md` (or documented equivalent); production/code paths `deny`. ## US-0123 — Per-role OpenCode model slug routing (multi-provider)
- user_visible: true
- Title: Assign per-role/per-phase OpenCode `provider/slug` including Chinese APIs without vendor IDs in template
- Summary: Cursor aliases (`fast`/`inherit`) do not give operators real vendors on subagents. Keys stay in OpenCode `/connect` (not git). Template files must not contain volatile vendor IDs. Unknown slug fails closed.

## US-0124 — Orchestrator plugin spawn-only `/auto` on OpenCode
- user_visible: true
- Title: OpenCode orchestrator plugin Task-spawns US-0069 roles, never executes phase work in-session
- Summary: On OpenCode the plugin **is** the native chain (do **not** port US-0095 Cursor Task-loop). `/auto` is spawn-only: resolve phase→role via **US-0069**, spawn an isolated child session, write isolation evidence, honor the **US-0092** stop matrix, and refuse orchestrator (or any role) performing another role’s artifact writes. Headless uses **US-0092** `--invoke-cmd`. Plugin API v1 vs v2 is research-locked (R-0109), not this intake. Success tests (a)(d): a model that ignores its prompt still cannot skip spawn isolation or continue `/auto` without the next role’s fresh session.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - Independently valuable: spawn-only `/auto` on OpenCode with isolation + stop matrix, even before thin command files exist (operators can still invoke the plugin/primary agent).
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0095 / DEC-0080**: **do not port** Cursor native chain. Plugin replaces that host mechanism.
  - **US-0092 / DEC-0078**: **compose** — reuse outer driver + `--invoke-cmd` + stop reasons; do not reimplement the state machine in TypeScript.
  - **US-0069**: **compose** — same phase→role matrix.
  - **US-0023 / BUG-0006**: **compose** — spawn-only; fail closed if stock OpenCode cannot isolate child sessions (thin fork is deferred `opencode-fork`, not silent same-session roleplay).
- Intake pack evidence (first-intake-pack, program bundle):
  - selected_pack: first-intake-pack
  - asked_topics: users_problem, runtime_target_environment, language_framework_runtime, architecture_preference, ui_design_expectations, security_compliance, non_functional_priorities, scope_timeline
  - missing_topics: (none)
  - assumptions_confirmed: Default install host remains cursor-only until explicit `--host opencode|both` opt-in; OpenCode plugin v1 vs v2 deferred to `/research`.
  - intake_evidence_ref: handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0121-intake-20260822.json
  - plan_area_coverage: `orchestrator-plugin-spawn` + `headless-invoke-cmd` → [US-0124]
  - coverage_complete: true
- Acceptance:
  - [ ] AC-1: **Spawn-only `/auto`** — orchestrator plugin/primary agent must not write phase artifacts (`docs/product/**`, `docs/engineering/**`, `sprints/**` phase outputs) in its own session. Attempt → fail-closed reason code (`AUTO_ORCHESTRATOR_PHASE_EXECUTION` analogue).
  - [ ] AC-2: **US-0069 resolve** — next phase maps to the matrix role; wrong-role spawn fails closed (`PHASE_ROLE_MISMATCH` analogue).
  - [ ] AC-3: **Isolation evidence** — each spawned session records `phase_id`, `role`, `fresh_context_marker`, timestamp (US-0023 / US-0048 pattern).
  - [ ] AC-4: **Success test (a)** — contract/harness proves a prompt-ignoring orchestrator still cannot skip spawn isolation (same-session roleplay is rejected).
  - [ ] AC-5: **Success test (d)** — `/auto` cannot continue to the next phase without a fresh session for the next role.
  - [ ] AC-6: **Stop matrix** — plugin/outer-driver honors US-0092 stop reasons (decision_gate, loop_max, blocked, pause). No silent continue.
  - [ ] AC-7: **Headless `--invoke-cmd`** — US-0092 outer driver can invoke OpenCode non-interactive/session API; when native in-session chain is unavailable, emit `NATIVE_CHAIN_UNAVAILABLE` analogue rather than roleplay.
  - [ ] AC-8: **Subtask-ignored fail-closed** — if OpenCode V2 command `subtask` (or equivalent) is ignored and child sessions cannot be isolated, fail closed with a documented `OPENCODE_*` reason code; do not degrade to one-chat multi-role (R-0001 / R-0109).
  - [ ] AC-9: **No US-0095 port** — `.cursor/commands/auto.md` Cursor Task-chain prose is not copied into the plugin. Cursor `/auto` remains for the Cursor host.
  - [ ] AC-10: **Contract tests** — `test_us0124_*` cover spawn-only deny, isolation evidence fields, stop-matrix wiring, `--invoke-cmd` hook, and subtask-ignored fail-closed.
  - [ ] AC-11: **Secrets** — plugin logs must not print API keys or `.env` contents (US-0085 posture).
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: orchestrator plugin, spawn/isolation, US-0069 mapping, stop matrix, `--invoke-cmd`, fail-closed codes, `test_us0124_*`.
  - Out of scope: reimplementing Python validators (US-0125), installer (US-0121), forking OpenCode unless research proves isolation impossible, sovereign-loop-on-opencode.

## US-0125 — Thin OpenCode commands and Python validator bridge
- user_visible: true
- Title: Named OpenCode commands are dispatch-only; Python validators remain fail-closed source of truth
- Summary: Layer 3 commands (`.opencode/commands/*.md`) are named entry points (`/intake`, `/execute`, `/auto`, …) that select the role agent, pass a short phase id + artifact path list, then **stop**. They must not clone Cursor 200-line command bodies. The plugin/CLI invokes existing `scripts/*_validate.py` gates; validators are **not** reimplemented in TypeScript. Success test (b): a model that ignores its prompt still cannot run `/release` after a failing validator.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - Independently valuable: operators get named slash commands plus hard validator gates even if they invoke phases manually.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0001**: **compose** — keep phase *names* and artifact outputs; do not triple-copy command files.
  - **US-0124**: plugin may call the same CLIs; this story owns the command files + the “Python is source of truth” contract.
- Intake pack evidence (first-intake-pack, program bundle):
  - selected_pack: first-intake-pack
  - asked_topics: users_problem, runtime_target_environment, language_framework_runtime, architecture_preference, ui_design_expectations, security_compliance, non_functional_priorities, scope_timeline
  - missing_topics: (none)
  - assumptions_confirmed: Default install host remains cursor-only until explicit `--host opencode|both` opt-in; OpenCode plugin v1 vs v2 deferred to `/research`.
  - intake_evidence_ref: handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0121-intake-20260822.json
  - plan_area_coverage: `validator-bridge` + `thin-commands` → [US-0125]
  - coverage_complete: true
- Acceptance:
  - [ ] AC-1: **Dispatch-only commands** — each named OpenCode command selects role + phase id + artifact path list and stops. No embedded 200-line Cursor procedure.
  - [ ] AC-2: **Clone guard** — contract test fails if `.opencode/commands/` copies `.cursor/commands/` bodies above a documented size/similarity threshold.
  - [ ] AC-3: **Validator source of truth** — persistence-blocking gates remain existing Python CLIs (`intake_evidence_validate.py`, `bug_issue_validate.py`, and other fail-closed validators already in the kit). Plugin/command may subprocess them; must not reimplement rules.
  - [ ] AC-4: **Success test (b)** — `/release` (or release persistence path) after a failing validator is blocked even if the command/agent prompt says to continue.
  - [ ] AC-5: **Fail-closed reason codes** — validator non-zero exit surfaces existing kit reason codes (or documented `OPENCODE_*` wrapper that still names the Python code). No silent skip.
  - [ ] AC-6: **If a rule can be a plugin check or Python CLI, it must not live in a command file** — grep/test for policy text that duplicates validator logic in commands.
  - [ ] AC-7: **Optional commands** — missing a convenience command must not disable plugin spawn (US-0124) or Python CLIs. Commands are Layer 3.
  - [ ] AC-8: **Contract tests** — `test_us0125_*` cover thin-command inventory, clone guard, validator subprocess fail-closed, and success test (b).
  - [ ] AC-9: **Compose US-0001** — Cursor command files unchanged. OpenCode commands are additive.
  - [ ] AC-10: **No new npm runtime in consumer app code** — validator bridge is kit scripts + plugin subprocess, not a dependency of the operator’s application.

  - In scope: thin `.opencode/commands/`, Python CLI bridge, clone/size guards, success test (b), `test_us0125_*`.

## US-0131 — Cross-host Its-Magic runtime configuration and parity
- user_visible: true
- Title: Cross-host Its-Magic runtime configuration and parity
- Summary: Ensure shared Its-Magic lifecycle and governance behavior is configured through a host-neutral runtime contract. Cursor keeps its scratchpad as a compatibility surface, while OpenCode-only installs must operate without `.cursor/`. Shared validators, phase transitions, artifact ownership, state/handoff handling, and installer preservation must resolve configuration deterministically in Cursor-only, OpenCode-only, and both-host installations. Host-specific features remain explicitly classified instead of being silently assumed to work everywhere.
- Priority: P1
- Status: DONE
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single cross-host story** — shared runtime configuration, host adapters, installer behavior, common-script refactoring, documentation, and contract tests form one usable vertical slice.
  - **Split rejected**: configuration without shared-script migration would leave OpenCode-only installs with a nominal config that the kernel still ignores; parity without an explicit host-neutral contract would preserve ambiguous ownership.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0073 / DEC-0055**: compose — existing Cursor scratchpad merge precedence remains available as a compatibility adapter; it is not silently redefined.
  - **US-0121..US-0126**: compose — OpenCode host pack, agents, commands, plugin, and runbook remain supported; this story closes cross-host runtime gaps rather than cloning Cursor files.
  - **US-0101 / US-0102 / US-0123**: compose — model routing remains host-specific and is specified separately by US-0132.
- Intake pack evidence (small-intake-pack):
  - selected_pack: small-intake-pack
  - asked_topics: outcome_success_criteria, impacted_components, constraints_compatibility_risks, required_tests_acceptance_checks, done_definition
  - missing_topics: (none)
  - assumptions_confirmed: (none)
  - intake_evidence_ref: handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0131-0132-intake-20260906.json
- Acceptance:
  - [ ] AC-1: **Host-neutral source of truth** — Define a documented, typed, host-neutral configuration contract for shared Its-Magic runtime and governance settings, with no credentials or provider secrets.
  - [ ] AC-2: **Cursor compatibility adapter** — Cursor scratchpad layers continue to work with their existing precedence and local-file protection while resolving shared settings through the host-neutral contract.
  - [ ] AC-3: **OpenCode-only operation** — An OpenCode-only install can resolve all shared settings required by its supported lifecycle without requiring `.cursor/scratchpad.md` or `.cursor/scratchpad.local.md`.
  - [ ] AC-4: **Shared-kernel migration** — Shared Python validators, outer-driver paths, state/handoff governance, and other common scripts accept the resolved configuration explicitly and do not silently hardcode `.cursor` for host-neutral behavior.
  - [ ] AC-5: **Host-specific boundaries** — Cursor-only capabilities and OpenCode-only capabilities are classified and fail or skip deterministically when unavailable; no command claims unsupported parity silently.
  - [ ] AC-6: **Both-host determinism** — `--host both` has one deterministic precedence model, prevents conflicting duplicate writes, and preserves independent host-local overrides where schemas differ.
  - [ ] AC-7: **Installer safety** — Install, missing, upgrade, and clean behavior delivers config examples to the selected host, preserves local operator files, and does not overwrite active scratchpad/config data.
  - [ ] AC-8: **Verification and documentation** — Add cross-host contract tests for cursor-only, opencode-only, and both-host modes; document supported lifecycle phases, config precedence, migration, and reason-code behavior.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: shared runtime configuration contract, Cursor compatibility reader, OpenCode adapter, common-script config injection, host matrix, installer preservation, tests, and operator documentation.
  - Out of scope: changing Cursor or OpenCode model schemas, adding provider proxies, cloning all Cursor command/rule bodies, and redesigning host-specific UX.

## US-0132 — Explicit Cursor/OpenCode model configuration contract
- user_visible: true
- Title: Explicit Cursor/OpenCode model configuration contract
- Summary: Remove ambiguity around model configuration files and precedence. Define which host owns `.cursor/model-catalog.local.json`, `.opencode/model-catalog.local.json`, `opencode.json{,c}`, and scratchpad `MODEL_*` keys; preserve separate Cursor tier/phase and OpenCode role/provider schemas; make materialization, validation, install delivery, and local-file protection deterministic. A generic `model.json` name must not become an undocumented third source of truth.
- Priority: P1
- Status: OPEN
- Decomposition (US-0051):
  - **Single model-contract story** — ownership, schemas, precedence, materializers, validators, installer delivery, docs, and cross-host tests must ship together so no host receives a model setting that its runtime ignores.
  - **Split rejected**: schema documentation without materialization would leave installed OpenCode agents unresolved; materialization without ownership rules would recreate the current `.cursor` versus `.opencode` ambiguity.
- Overlap / duplicate evaluation:
  - **US-0101 / DEC-0086**: compose — Cursor tier and phase resolution remains unchanged.
  - **US-0102 / DEC-0087**: compose — Cursor role catalog and volatile-ID protections remain unchanged.
  - **US-0123 / DEC-0123**: compose — OpenCode keeps its per-role `provider/slug` catalog and does not consume Cursor scratchpad model keys.
  - **US-0131**: compose — shared runtime configuration is supplied by the cross-host contract; model resolution remains a host-specific adapter.
- Intake pack evidence (small-intake-pack):
  - selected_pack: small-intake-pack
  - asked_topics: outcome_success_criteria, impacted_components, constraints_compatibility_risks, required_tests_acceptance_checks, done_definition
  - missing_topics: (none)
  - assumptions_confirmed: (none)
  - intake_evidence_ref: handoffs/intake_evidence/US-0131-0132-intake-20260906.json
- Acceptance:
  - [ ] AC-1: **Canonical ownership** — Document and validate the supported model configuration inventory: Cursor `.cursor/model-catalog.local.json` and `MODEL_*` scratchpad keys, OpenCode `.opencode/model-catalog.local.json`, and local-only `opencode.json{,c}` options. An undocumented generic `model.json` path is rejected or explicitly mapped.
  - [ ] AC-2: **Separate schemas** — Cursor keeps tier/phase/role-catalog semantics; OpenCode keeps per-role `provider/slug` semantics. Neither runtime interprets the other host's catalog as its own.
  - [ ] AC-3: **Deterministic precedence** — Define precedence independently for each host, including direct overrides, catalogs, defaults, absent catalogs, and `--host both`; precedence must be observable in diagnostics.
  - [ ] AC-4: **Materialization correctness** — OpenCode local catalog values materialize idempotently into installed agents only; Cursor resolution remains compatible; templates never receive operator slugs or credentials.
  - [ ] AC-5: **Fail-closed validation** — Present but malformed, undeclared, empty, or unknown model configuration fails with the correct host-scoped reason code; absent optional configuration follows a documented default and is never confused with invalid configuration.
  - [ ] AC-6: **Local-file protection** — Install, upgrade, missing, and clean paths preserve active local catalogs, scratchpad overrides, and local OpenCode config according to explicit host ownership rules.
  - [ ] AC-7: **Triple-surface parity** — Python, PowerShell, and shell installers, validators, manifest entries, and template examples agree on model-file delivery and protection behavior for all host modes.
  - [ ] AC-8: **Contract tests and operator docs** — Add tests for schema separation, precedence, unknown/absent behavior, materialization, secret/template hygiene, both-host coexistence, and document the exact model configuration recipes and migration path.
- Boundaries:
  - In scope: model configuration names and ownership, Cursor/OpenCode schemas, precedence, validators, materializers, installer behavior, examples, tests, and runbook/README documentation.

### BUG-0008 ? Global Linux install fails: empty `install_include_paths` when manifest is CRLF
- user_visible: true
- Status: DONE
- environment: Debian Linux (Docker host `docker-dmz`); global npm **`its-magic@0.1.2-40`**; **`/usr/lib/node_modules/its-magic/template/docs/engineering/context/installer-owned-paths.manifest`** shows **`^M$`** per **`cat -A`**.
- steps_to_reproduce: 1. **`npm install -g its-magic`** (package built/published with CRLF manifest lines). 2. Run **`its-magic --target <repo> --mode missing`** (or equivalent). 3. Observe **`[INSTALL_MANIFEST_ERROR] install_include_paths section is empty`** despite visible path lines in the manifest file.

### BUG-0009 ? its-magic ships its OWN packaging CI into generated repos, breaking CI in every created project
- user_visible: true
- Status: DONE
- environment: Any repository created/installed with `its-magic` (reported across all such repos; concrete example `finance_goblin` on GitHub Actions, Ubuntu + Windows runners). Affected file copied into targets: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (from packaged `template/.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Installer copy path declared in `docs/engineering/context/installer-owned-paths.manifest` (`[install_include_paths]` `.github/workflows`; `[clean_paths]` `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`).
- steps_to_reproduce: 1. Install its-magic into a new project (`its-magic --mode missing` / `--create`) or upgrade an existing one. 2. Push to GitHub so the copied `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs. 3. Observe the `npm-test`, `brew-test`, and `choco-test` jobs fail in the target repo even though the project is not its-magic itself.
- expected: A generated/installed project receives only generic, project-agnostic CI (the runbook-driven `checks` + `auto-fix` jobs). its-magic's own distribution/self-packaging jobs (`npm pack its-magic-*.tgz`, `sh installer.sh`, `packaging/chocolatey` choco pack, `packaging/homebrew` brew style) must NOT be copied into downstream repos, and must not run there. New installs/upgrades produce a CI workflow that is green-by-default for a fresh project, and the generic `checks` job does not hard-fail merely because a fresh project has no real tests/lint configured yet.
- actual: `template/.github/workflows/ci.yml` is byte-identical to its-magic's own `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and includes the self-packaging jobs `npm-test` (`npm pack` ? expects `its-magic-*.tgz` / `package.json`), `brew-test` (`sh installer.sh ...`), and `choco-test` (`Push-Location packaging/chocolatey; choco pack`). None of those paths exist in a downstream project, so the workflow fails in every its-magic-created repo: `npm error enoent Could not read package.json` (exit 254); `sh: installer.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127); `Push-Location : Cannot find path '...\packaging\chocolatey'` (exit 1). Additionally the generic `checks` job can fail with `Tests or lint failed` for fresh projects with no real tests/lint.
- evidence_refs: user report (2026-06-06) with GitHub Actions logs from `finance_goblin` (`npm pack` ENOENT package.json exit 254; `sh installer.sh` No such file exit 127; `Push-Location packaging/chocolatey` PathNotFound exit 1; `Tests or lint failed` exit 1); `template/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (jobs `npm-test`, `brew-test`, `choco-test`); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (identical source); `docs/engineering/context/installer-owned-paths.manifest`; `installer.ps1`; `installer.sh`; `installer.py`; `handoffs/intake_evidence/BUG-0009-intake-20260606.json` (`python scripts/intake_evidence_validate.py --file handoffs/intake_evidence/BUG-0009-intake-20260606.json` ? `[INTAKE_EVIDENCE_VALIDATION_OK]`).
- intake_notes (2026-06-06, PO, Cursor, `cursor-20260606-BUG0009-intake`, `/intake bug`, `INTAKE_GUIDED_MODE=1`): Captured as a packaging/template-leak defect. Root cause hypothesis (for `/discovery` to confirm): the active repo's CI and the downstream template CI were kept identical, so its-magic-only distribution jobs (`npm-test`/`brew-test`/`choco-test`) leak into every generated repo. No CI-parity guard currently enforces `template/.github/workflows/ci.yml == .github/workflows/ci.yml` (only intake-script parity is guarded via `scripts/check_intake_template_parity.py`), so the template CI can be safely decoupled. Operator scope decisions (asked this run): (1) fix targets new installs/upgrades only ? existing broken repos heal on their next its-magic upgrade since `upgrade`/`clean` modes re-copy the corrected `ci.yml`; (2) also include hardening so the generic `checks` job is tolerant/clear when a fresh project has no real tests yet. Proposed fix direction (defer exact design to architecture): split CI into a downstream-safe template workflow (generic `checks` + `auto-fix` only, runbook-driven, no self-packaging jobs) vs its-magic's own internal CI (keep `npm-test`/`brew-test`/`choco-test` for self-distribution), and add a regression/drift guard that fails if the template CI references its-magic self-packaging paths. **Status: OPEN** per **US-0045**. **Next**: `/discovery` (fresh PO context) for `BUG-0009`.

### BUG-0010 ? Architecture triad archiver ignores `## US-xxxx` headings, blocking `/auto` with `STATE_ARCHIVE_BOUNDARY_AMBIGUOUS`
- user_visible: true
- Status: DONE
- environment: its-magic workflow in downstream repos using triad hot-surface enforcement (**DEC-0054** / **US-0072**); concrete operator report during `/auto` after successful discovery on **US-0016** (root README story). `docs/engineering/architecture.md` exceeded `ARCH_HOT_MAX_LINES` (reported **3021** lines vs cap **3000** in operator repo); story sections authored as **`## US-xxxx`** H2 headings. Triad gate invoked post-phase (`python scripts/enforce-triad-hot-surface.py --check` / `--rollover`).
- steps_to_reproduce: 1. Use its-magic in a repo where `docs/engineering/architecture.md` grows past `ARCH_HOT_MAX_LINES` with story sections written as `## US-xxxx ...` (no or insufficient `# US-xxxx` H1 split boundaries). 2. Run `/auto` through a phase that triggers the triad gate (for example discovery completes and appends handoff material). 3. Observe `--rollover` cannot archive: `split_arch_stories` finds zero `STORY_HEADING` matches (`^# US-\d{4}` only). 4. `--check` / gate fails with `STATE_ARCHIVE_BOUNDARY_AMBIGUOUS` or `ARTIFACT_HOT_SURFACE_OVERSIZE`; `/auto` stops with non-suppressible `blocked`.
- expected: Triad rollover archives oldest story sections when `architecture.md` exceeds line or section caps, regardless of whether historical sections used H2 (`## US-xxxx`) or H1 (`# US-xxxx`) ? per operator-facing **DEC-0054** intent that architecture story sections are archival units. New `/architecture` writes should enforce H1 `# US-xxxx` boundaries going forward. `/auto` must not block on pre-existing `## US-` repos once fix ships.
- actual: `scripts/enforce-triad-hot-surface.py` `STORY_HEADING` regex matches only H1 `# US-\d{4}\s*[:\u2014\-]`; `## US-xxxx` sections are invisible to `split_arch_stories`. When the file is over cap but `stories=[]`, rollover raises `STATE_ARCHIVE_BOUNDARY_AMBIGUOUS` ("architecture file exceeds line cap but has no US story headings to archive"). Operators cannot auto-unblock without manual heading rewrite, manual archive, or bumping `ARCH_HOT_MAX_LINES` in scratchpad.
